DECISION: IMPROVE

The proved rate is sound, but the paper is not mathematically maximized. Its restriction to a known uniform half-disc and radial outcome regressions is unnecessary. The same frontier extends to a substantially broader and more faithful boundary-discontinuity class with unknown design, curved boundaries, and angle-varying bivariate regression functions. This is a material headline/scope improvement, not a cosmetic strengthening.

Precise directive:

1. Replace the current radial class by a superclass in which:

   - assignment is sharp across any known boundary through b;
   - Y(t) is Bernoulli with side-specific mean μ_t(x);
   - μ_t extends to b, takes values in [1/4,3/4], and is L-Lipschitz in x on its treatment-side neighborhood;
   - the unknown design satisfies only a two-sided local-mass condition P(T=t, ‖X-b‖<H) ≥ c₀H² for t∈{0,1} and all H≤1/2.

   Continue to observe exactly Z_Δ=(Y,T,Δ⌊‖X-b‖/Δ⌋), with neither X, angle, nor raw radius observed.

2. Replace the known-probability estimator S_t/(np) by the observed-count estimator. Let N_t = Σ_i 1{T_i=t, Q_Δ(R_i)<H}, S_t = Σ_i 1{T_i=t, Q_Δ(R_i)<H}Y_i. Use S_t/N_t when N_t>0, with any fixed clipped fallback when N_t=0. Conditional on N_t, S_t is binomial with success probability equal to the local side average. Lipschitz continuity gives bias at most LH because every retained X lies within H of b. Standard binomial inverse-moment bounds and the local-mass condition give absolute risk O(H+(nH²)^−1/2) and squared risk O(H²+(nH²)^−1), hence the same max{n^−1/4,Δ} frontier for H=Δ⌈n^−1/4/Δ⌉.

3. Make the interval conditional-count exact: apply Clopper–Pearson to S_t∣N_t, define the mean interval as [0,1] when N_t=0, enlarge each side by LH, and difference the side intervals. Chernoff splitting at N_t≈np_t gives expected length O((np_t)^−1/2+LH)=O(max{n^−1/4,Δ}), while the interval remains defined on every sample.

4. Retain the existing uniform half-disc radial Bernoulli laws as an embedded subclass for the converse. The existing single alternative g(r)=κ{(h-r)_+ + Δφ(r/Δ)1(r<Δ)} then proves the lower bound over the larger class by subclass→superclass minimax transfer. It is irrelevant that φ is not orthogonal for every unknown nonuniform design: a minimax lower bound needs one legal same-design pair, and the uniform radial pair already supplies it. Thus the current “technical internal limitation” incorrectly rules out a valid scope transfer.

5. Synchronize the TL;DR, project justification, related work, honest scope, theorem statements, and consumer text. The revised headline should say that the frontier holds over an unknown-design, bivariate Lipschitz boundary class, with the uniform half-disc used only as the least-favorable subclass. Do not claim that exact aliasing occurs under every admissible design.

Mathematical audit of the current proof:

- The same-class lower genuinely combines sampling and aliasing in one pair. The Δ component has zero first-bin r-weighted mean and contributes no released likelihood divergence; the h=n^−1/4 triangular bump alone contributes χ²=O(h⁴), so its n-fold divergence stays bounded. The target displacement is κ(h+Δ), uniformly at least κ max{h,Δ}.
- Both laws satisfy the present Lipschitz and Bernoulli-range restrictions. No assumption posits the null direction, testing distance, or desired rate, so the crux is not laundered.
- The achievability proof correctly uses H as a quantizer boundary, p=H²/2, bias 2LH/3, and variance at most 1/(np).
- The exact-binomial interval is total, including zero and all-success counts. Its coverage uses only marginal Clopper–Pearson coverage and a union bound, so dependence of the two side counts causes no issue.
- All Δ regimes are covered: Δ≤h, Δ≈h, and Δ≫h. There is no missing rate elbow; a fixed transition ratio Δn^1/4 changes constants, not order. A sharp transition constant would be a separate high-effort project.
- Minor non-headline cleanup: the codomain stated for the minimax expected length should be [0,∞), not [0,1], and the honest class should explicitly require closed bounded interval-valued maps.

Comparator/class audit:

- Cattaneo–Titiunik–Yu is not the same class. Its main assumptions include an observed bivariate score with continuous positive density, smooth bivariate conditional means, a rectifiable boundary, an exact distance metric, kernel/Gram regularity, and shrinking-bandwidth asymptotics. Its Theorem 6 instead considers exact-radius estimators and uniform loss along a rectifiable boundary over a Hölder bivariate regression class. A representative hypothesis is “μ(x) belongs to a Hölder ball of smoothness q.” This is neither the present fixed-point Bernoulli minimax experiment nor its model class. No published lower bound transfers literally to the current theorem. The paper is a rate/method comparator only. Primary source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.26051.
- Dong (2015) is not the same class. Theorem 1 assumes a scalar latent running variable, correct side classification, identifiable cell means, identified rounding-error moments, and that the side regressions “are polynomials of possibly unknown degree J.” Its triangular inversion therefore does not subsume a nonparametric annular nullspace. Primary author PDF: https://yingyingdong.com/Research/Dong_JAE_2015.pdf.
- Kolesár–Rothe (2018) studies an intrinsically discrete scalar running variable and local-polynomial inference. Its honest construction assumes the conditional mean is twice differentiable on each side with bounded second derivative. It has no latent within-annulus observation operator or radial mass law. Primary source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.04086.
- Armstrong–Kolesár (2018) gives abstract modulus/optimal-CI machinery for a linear functional over a convex regression class; finite-sample results use the hypothesis that “regression errors are normal, with known variance.” It supplies proof logic, not the same Bernoulli random-design experiment or an evaluated rounded-radius modulus. Primary source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.06028.
- Armstrong–Kolesár (2020) studies kernel/local-polynomial estimators under Taylor or Hölder derivative bounds; in its terminology, “the case p=1 corresponds to the Lipschitz class.” Its principal procedures are bias-aware asymptotic/nonparametric-regression intervals, not total conditional-binomial intervals under radial coarsening. Primary source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.01200.
- Dong–Kolesár (2023) assumes the observed scalar score correctly classifies assignment and its potential-outcome conditional means are smooth; its identified target is the effect conditional on the observed score at the cutoff, not the latent fixed spatial point effect here. Primary source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.07388.

Faithfulness concern:

The phrases “exact-radius reduction” and “familiar pointwise radial Lipschitz scale” should not imply that Cattaneo–Titiunik–Yu proved the same pointwise minimax theorem. Their Theorem 4 supplies the exact-distance stochastic scale, while their Theorem 6 is a uniform-along-boundary lower bound for a different class and loss. Rename the proposition “fine-quantization regime” and describe the anchor as a rate sanity check. The current theorem is not a restatement of any cited result.

The required iteration is therefore the superclass/count-normalized reformulation above. It preserves the existing least-favorable construction and rate while removing two unnecessary restrictions and materially improving the paper’s headline and field relevance.
